content: Before starting treatment with this medication, during its use, and for some time after completing the treatment, it is essential to undergo regular medical and laboratory tests. These tests may include a complete blood count, kidney function, liver function, thyroid function, and blood pressure monitoring. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to take it as soon as possible according to the prescribed schedule. Do not skip doses unless directed by your healthcare provider. This medication does not require specific storage instructions. Your medical condition may lead to complications during a medical emergency. It is important to inform healthcare providers about your condition and any medications you are taking. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, stomach or abdominal pain, fatigue, headache, tremors, difficulty sleeping, or mouth sores. However, this medication may also cause serious side effects. It has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. This medication may increase the risk of a rare but potentially fatal brain infection called progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before receiving this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using this medication before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. This medication may increase your risk of developing a serious infection caused by the bacteria Listeria. During treatment and for some time afterward, avoid foods that may contain Listeria, such as deli meats, unpasteurized milk and cheese products, soft cheeses, and undercooked meat, seafood, or poultry. Alternatively, ensure these foods are thoroughly heated before consumption. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby. Your doctor will likely order a pregnancy test before starting treatment. Discuss reliable forms of birth control to use during treatment and for at least three months after the last dose. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for at least three months after the last dose. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669.
